steps.description: Take the given ray PQ. Draw an arc of some radius taking point P as its centre, which intersects PQ at R.

question_text: Construct an equilateral triangle, given its side and justify the construction.

question_image.description: Diagram showing the construction steps for an equilateral triangle.

answer_text: Let us draw an equilateral triangle of side 5 cm. We know that all sides of an equilateral triangle are equal. Therefore, all sides of the equilateral triangle will be 5 cm. We also know that each angle of an equilateral triangle is 60º. The below given steps will be followed to draw an equilateral triangle of 5 cm side.

steps.description: Draw a line segment AB of 5 cm length.
Draw an arc of some radius, while taking A as its centre. Let it intersect AB at P.
Taking P as centre, draw an arc to intersect the previous arc at E. Join AE.
Taking A as centre, draw an arc of 5 cm radius, which intersects extended line segment AE at C. Join AC and BC.

final_answer: Therefore, ∆ABC is the required equilateral triangle of side 5 cm.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of basic geometric construction and justification.

question_text: Justification of Construction: We can justify the construction by showing ABC as an equilateral triangle i.e., AB = BC = AC = 5 cm and A = B = C = 60°.

question_image.description: Diagram showing triangle ABC with equal sides and angles.

answer_text: In ∆ABC, we have AC = AB = 5 cm and A = 60°. Since AC = AB, B = C (Angles opposite to equal sides of a triangle). In ∆ABC, A + B + C = 180° (Angle sum property of a triangle). 60° + C + C = 180°; 60° + 2C = 180°; 2C = 120°; C = 60°; B = C = 60°. We have, A = B = C = 60°.
final_answer: From equations (1) and (2), ∆ABC is an equilateral triangle.
